title: Inference prospect engagement framework and pricing scenarios 2026
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
OVERVIEW

Purpose: This playbook is a pragmatic engagement framework for reps and solutions engineers to position Redwood Inference during mid-to-large prospect cycles. It combines: concise messaging, competitive differentiation, three pricing scenarios with example math, a pitch-deck outline with speaker notes, a compact case study, a security FAQ tailored to prospect concerns, and objection-handling scripts. Use this as a living doc — update pricing examples with current rate cards and redirect technical questions to eng-se or product-ops.

Target personas
- Head of ML / ML Platform: cost/operationalization, model versioning, SLAs.
- Backend / Product Engineering Lead: latency, integration effort, SDKs, API stability.
- Security / Infra: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, compliance evidence.
- Procurement / Finance: predictable spend, reserved options, contract terms.

TOP-LINE MESSAGING (1-sentence and 3-line)
- 1-sentence: Redwood Inference provides a single runtime and control plane to serve LLMs with production reliability, predictable economics, and a unified developer experience across hosted, reserved, and private deployments.
- 3-line: Ship LLM features fast with our hosted API, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost, and adopt Private for regulated or air-gapped needs — all with per-route observability, rollouts, and cost controls to avoid surprise bills.

POSITIONING & VALUE HYPOTHESES
- Cost predictability: Dedicated/reserved capacity with predictable token throughput reduces variable spend for high-volume inference (customers routinely see 20–60% lower per-token costs vs fully hosted on high-throughput workloads).
- Latency & reliability: GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart batching and KV caching deliver consistent p95/p99 latency; we support automatic model fallbacks and multi-region routing to meet SLAs.
- Developer productivity: Single API + SDKs and rollout primitives (canary/A-B/fallback) enable teams to iterate without bespoke infra.
- Compliance & isolation: Private deployments provide a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and audit trails for regulated workloads.

USE-CASE MESSAGING (30–60s per vertical)
- Customer Support Automation: Reduce avg handle time by 25–40% (RAG + tuned generation). Position: hosted for pilot, Dedicated when throughput hits 50 concurrent sessions.
- Search & Reranking: Improve relevance metrics and reduce expensive downstream compute via embeddings + reranker; latency SLOs of <150ms for p95.
- Knowledge & Summarization for Regulated Data: Private deployment + HSM + retention controls; emphasize auditability and deterministic model versions.

PRICING SCENARIOS (EXAMPLE NUMBERS FOR DISCUSSION)
Notes: These are template scenarios — replace with current rate card when quoting. All prices are illustrative and in USD.
1) Proof-of-concept (pilot, hosted)
- Assumptions: 1M tokens / month generation, 50k embeddings/month, 3-month pilot.
- Host rates (example): text gen $0.0006 / token, embeddings $0.00075 / unit.
- Monthly: gen = 1,000,000 * $0.0006 = $600; embeddings = 50,000 * $0.00075 = $37.50; estimated monthly = ~$637.50.
- Sales hook: Fast time-to-value, free tiers/credits to reduce friction.

2) Scale (growth SaaS using Hosted + caching)
- Assumptions: 100M tokens / month, caching reduces 40% effective tokens, embeddings 1M/month.
- Effective tokens billed = 60M.
- Hosted enterprise negotiated rate (example): $0.00035 / token; embeddings $0.0005 / unit.
- Monthly: gen = 60,000,000 * $0.00035 = $21,000; embeddings = 1,000,000 * $0.0005 = $500; total = ~$21,500.
- Levers to reduce cost: enable prefix/KV caching, batch config tuning, use quantized smaller model variants for non-sensitive workloads.

3) Predictable/Committed (Dedicated reserved capacity)
- Assumptions: Customer commits to a 3-node A100-equivalent pool (reserved) supporting 400M tokens / month baseline; burst to shared capacity allowed.
- Pricing: reserved capacity = monthly platform + reserved GPU commit. Example: platform fee $4,500 / mo + reserved node equivalent $12,000 / node / mo => 3 nodes = $36,000.
- Effective unit economics: with 400M tokens baseline, per-token baseline = ($40,500 / 400M) = $0.000101 / token — excluding embeddings and overage.
- Sales hook: predictable monthly capex/opex, SLA-backed latency and availability, better total cost at scale.

COST-REDUCTION RECOMMENDATIONS (for SEs/CS to propose)
- Deploy prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated context tokens by 30–70% depending on workflow.
- Use batching aggressively for back-of-house jobs; tune batching thresholds to balance latency/throughput.
- Quantize models for non-sensitive workloads where quality impact is acceptable.
- Route low-priority or long-context jobs to cheaper model variants or off-peak capacity.

COMPETITIVE BRIEF (top competitors and positioning)
Format: Competitor — What they sell — Redwood angle to win
- OpenAI (hosted-first, broad dev ecosystem) — Strengths: wide adoption, strong baseline models; Weaknesses: price variability at scale, less control for private/enterprise on-prem. Redwood angle: predictable economics (Dedicated), private deployments, and clear performance profiles + observability.
- Anthropic / Claude (safety-first models) — Strengths: model safety and contextual handling; Weaknesses: enterprise integration and on-prem options vary. Redwood angle: flexibility to host/serve multiple model families, rollouts and regressions guardrails for productized safety testing.
- Vector DB + ML infra stacks (self-hosted: TorchServe, KServe, BentoML) — Strengths: total control, cost at large scale; Weaknesses: operational burden, engineering time. Redwood angle: unified runtime + ops tooling removes engineering overhead while preserving control in Private.
- Cloud-managed endpoints by hyperscalers (GCP/AWS model endpoints) — Strengths: deep infra integration; Weaknesses: fragmented tooling for LLM-specific optimizations. Redwood angle: LLM-optimized runtime, quantization recommendations, and per-route cost/latency observability.

BATTLECARD: Objections and concise rebuttals
- "We can just use OpenAI / hyperscaler APIs and be done." -> Rebuttal: For pilots yes; but at scale you’ll face unit cost creep and less control for regulated or latency-sensitive apps. We provide a migration path and predictable reserved pricing to manage spend and SLAs.
- "We need full control / will self-host." -> Rebuttal: Self-hosting avoids vendor lock but duplicates years of operational investment. Redwood Private gives control + hardened ops templates (onprem packaging + day-2 ops) with productized rollouts and support.
- "How do we know model regressions won't break UX?" -> Rebuttal: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring + evals to rollouts so you can gate deployments on prompt-set metrics and trigger automatic rollback.

PITCH DECK: 10-slide outline + speaker notes (concise)
1. Title / TL;DR: What Redwood does and one-sentence customer outcome. (Speaker note: set the economic frame — lower cost per request, predictable SLAs).
2. Customer problem: unpredictable inference costs, brittle rollouts, and ops overhead. (Note: use prospect-specific metrics if available).
3. Product overview: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private + Console. (Note: diagram showing same API across deployment modes).
4. Performance & economics: benchmarks (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost curves). (Note: reference our model catalog/verified profiles).
5. Case studies / outcomes (one-slide): key metric lifts and timelines.
6. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC/ISO evidence. (Note: emphasize Private and turnkey evidence).
7. Integration & migration path: pilot -> dedicated -> private, plus SDKs & templates. (Note: propose a 6–8 week path).
8. Pricing options and example scenarios (use the pricing scenarios above). (Note: include TCO snapshot).
9. Go-to-production (SLA, support tiers, onboarding). (Note: highlight Technical Account Manager + playbook delivery).
10. Next steps & ask (pilot proposal, architecture workshop, POC success criteria). (Note: end with clear CTA).

SAMPLE CASE STUDY (1-page summary)
Title: Observability SaaS reduced inference costs and improved p95 latency
Customer: AtlasTrace (mid-market SaaS observability vendor) — anonymized
Challenge: At 20M tokens/month, variable costs and p95 generation latency were causing customer churn for the trial experience.
Approach: Pilot on Hosted API for 4 weeks, then moved heavy inference to Dedicated reserved pool + enabled prefix caching and smaller quantized reranker for lower-cost pages.
Outcome (30 days post-migration): 42% reduction in per-token spend vs baseline, p95 latency improved from 420ms to 140ms for web-facing flows, and time-to-resolution for technical support decreased by 18%.
Quote: "Redwood let us iterate quickly and then lock in predictable economics when scale mattered." — Head of Platform, AtlasTrace

SECURITY FAQ (prospect-facing, concise answers)
Q: What deployment modes are available and which is right for regulated data?
A: Hosted API (fastest path to value), Dedicated (reserved, isolated GPU pools), Private (customer-managed control plane for VPC/on-prem). For regulated data we recommend Private with KMS and audit logging.
Q: How do you handle encryption and key management?
A: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+/mTLS for service-to-service. At-rest encryption supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments.
Q: Are audit logs and model usage trails available?
A: Yes — the Console exposes per-token usage logs, model version histories, who invoked routes, and retention options for audit export.
Q: What certifications/compliance artifacts can you provide?
A: We publish SOC2 Type II report excerpts and can provide architecture diagrams and control narratives. For regulated customers we offer an evidence package and an on-boarding compliance checklist.
Q: How do you protect against data exfiltration in model outputs?
A: Multiple layers: route-based policies, token redaction hooks, output filters, and optional private deployments that keep data in customer networks. We pair that with evals and regression testing on prompt sets to detect unexpected memorization.

SALES PLAY: 6–8 WEEK ENGAGEMENT PATH (recommended)
1) Week 0–1: Discovery + success criteria (data volumes, latency targets, compliance constraints).
2) Week 1–3: Pilot (Hosted): sample integration using SDKs, minimal data, measure latencies/costs, run baseline evals.
3) Week 3–5: Architecture workshop (Dedicated vs Private), sizing guidance, draft MSA/commit terms.
4) Week 5–8: Onboard Dedicated or Private, migrate traffic, enable optimize knobs (caching, batching), and run QA/eval guardrails.

OBJECTIONS & ONE-LINERS (cheat-sheet)
- "Too expensive" -> "We offer Reserved capacity and engineering best-practices that often reduce total cost by 20–60% compared to unmanaged hosted spend at scale."
- "Integration will take forever" -> "Most customers complete a pilot in 1–3 weeks using our SDKs and integration templates; Dedicated onboarding is a 4–8 week engagement with a TAM."

OPERATIONS & HANDOFFS
- SEs should deliver: pilot success criteria doc, sample prompt set (for evals), perf baseline, and a sizing worksheet.
- Post-sale handoff to CS: include reserved commit details, SLA ladder, runbooks, and rollout policy.

APPENDIX: SIZING CHECKLIST (quick)
- Expected qps and average response tokens per request
- Concurrent sessions and burst profile
- Retention/retention rules for KV/prefix caches
- Compliance requirements (e.g., data residency, encryption, audit retention)
- Preferred deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
